name: VLTG // Pressure Drop Tour Tee
description:
The tour shirt for VLTG's 2199 Pressure Drop run — a seven-city circuit through the mid-stacks and two Shelf-level venues that became legendary for a performance at Stack 9 where the power grid failed mid-set and the band played the last forty minutes acoustic, screaming into the dark. The shirt is black, always black, with the VLTG double-slash logo in a corroded white on the chest and the tour dates printed down the left sleeve in a tiny font that's already hard to read after one wash. The back has a stylized pressure gauge graphic cracked down the middle, the needle buried past the red.

Made by a screen printer in the Midmarket district who has done all of VLTG's merch since the beginning. 100% synth-cotton, pre-washed so it's soft from the start. This is a garment that means something if you were there. If you weren't, wearing one is a statement that will be checked.
what_it_says: You were at Stack 9. Or you know someone who was, and they gave this to you. Either way, you're placing a bet on your credibility.
worn_by: people who were at the Pressure Drop tour
story_hooks: A counterfeit run of Pressure Drop tees appeared three months after the tour, nearly identical but with the Stack 9 date wrong by one day — suggesting the counterfeiter had inside information but not quite enough.
The lead singer of VLTG was arrested six weeks after the tour ended. The shirt is now something people wear to the ongoing protests outside the Vantablack detention facility where she's being held.
A Tier 5 collector has been quietly purchasing original tour shirts for Φ400 each through a proxy buyer. Nobody knows why. VLTG's management finds this deeply unsettling.
related_entities: Ouroboros Energy Power Distribution Trunk Network

physical_description.visual_profile: Relaxed, vintage-worn band tee silhouette with understated graphic presence. Black foundation reads as genuinely lived-in rather than mass-produced. The corroded white logo and fragmented back graphic create an impression of authenticity and edge without aggression.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through shoulders and torso, not oversized but comfortable. Sleeves fall naturally. Cut suggests function over fashion, though proportions are contemporary—not baggy.
physical_description.primary_material: 100% synth-cotton, pre-washed and broken in. Soft hand, breathable, shows wear honestly.
physical_description.texture: Smooth surface with slight fading at stress points. Print has slight cracking and degradation visible even new—intentional distressing that mimics genuine aging. Sleeve print is already fading to nearly illegible, adding temporal authenticity.
physical_description.color_scheme: Pure black body with corroded/oxidized white graphics. Back pressure gauge features aged white with black cracking/shadowing effect suggesting mechanical failure and entropy.
distinctive_features: VLTG double-slash logo centered on chest in corroded white
Tour dates printed in tiny, deliberately hard-to-read font down left sleeve
Back graphic: stylized pressure gauge with needle buried past red zone, cracked vertically down center
Pre-distressed print mimicking natural wear and fading
Halftone Collective screen printer mark (discrete, back neck tag area)
Fabric slightly pilled at collar/cuff from intended aging
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 functional with subcultural capital. Not expensive, but valuable within specific community. Signals music scene participation, mid-stack cultural awareness, and possible direct event attendance.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing this marks participation in underground music culture of the GLMZ. The Stack 9 acoustic set is urban legend—this shirt proves you were part of that moment or aspire to that cultural moment. Sub-corporatist, anti-mainstream, but not aggressively so. Street credibility through genuine attachment.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in immediately. Already showing fade and slight print cracking. Meant to look like it has history even unworn. Further wear adds rather than detracts from its value.
